toml:
# The whole solar system at one epoch.
#
# Every body the engine knows — the Sun, the eight planets, Pluto, the Moon, Phobos,
# Deimos, Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto and Titan — at 2026-09-28 00:00 UTC: its
# heliocentric position and velocity in the ICRF (International Celestial Reference
# Frame, equatorial J2000), its physical constants (gravitational parameter, radii, J2 — the
# second zonal harmonic — where published, sidereal rotation, International Astronomical
# Union (IAU) pole, its J2000 mean value, and prime meridian at the epoch), the light time and one-way and
# two-way range from the Earth, and an orbit track sampled over one revolution.
# result.json carries enough to draw an interactive solar system.
#
# WHERE THE NUMBERS COME FROM
#   planets  Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Keplerian elements (Standish and Williams),
#            Table 1 for 1800 AD to 2050 AD
#   Moon     the Montenbruck & Gill lunar series, splitting the Earth-Moon barycentre
#   moons    JPL mean elements with the IAU synchronous rotation rate; Titan from the IAU
#            rotation model
#   light    the radiometric light-time solve, transmitter at its retarded position
#
# WHAT IS VALIDATED, AND WHAT IS NOT
# Each body carries its own label. Mercury to Saturn and the Earth are VALIDATED against
# JPL Horizons (Development Ephemeris DE441) within twice the Standish page's nominal
# error. Uranus and Neptune from Table 1 exceed the page's figures against DE441 (by 2.0
# and 5.2 times) and are MODELLED; so are Pluto, the Moon and the seven moons, which
# were measured against Horizons but have no published bound. See tests/solar_system_horizons_reference.rs.
#
# The three links below add the Mars-to-Jupiter, Saturn-to-Earth and Europa-to-Jupiter
# light times: interplanetary relay geometry, a ringed-planet downlink and a moon-to-planet
# hop.
kind = "solar-system"
epoch = "2026-09-28T00:00:00"
observer = "Earth"
track_points = 180

[[links]]
from = "Mars"
to = "Jupiter"

[[links]]
from = "Saturn"
to = "Earth"

[[links]]
from = "Europa"
to = "Jupiter"
